regulatory_and_risk_profile: Zero data retention (ZDR) and bring-your-own keys
Model Risk Management validation before any production use
paper_process_blockers: InfoSec review must run in parallel with the proof of value, not after it
Legal redlines on the data processing agreement take 90 days or more
Procurement needs a named budget owner before it issues a PO
Model Risk Management must sign off on any model used in credit or fraud decisions
dominant_friction: Risk committees block anything they cannot audit, even when the business case is strong.
value_frame: Lead with deterministic auditability, private VPC or ZDR architecture, and parallel InfoSec timelines before the proof of value completes.

buying_committee.primary_fear: We approve a model we cannot validate, reproduce, or defend to examiners.
Another pilot becomes shelfware that we must support forever.
A model leaks customer data through a sub-processor nobody reviewed.
An unexplained AI decision in a credit or fraud case becomes a regulatory finding.

signature_objections: Our CISO will not sign until zero data retention is written into the data processing agreement. Can you commit to that on paper this quarter?
If the model hallucinates a credit decision, who carries the liability, you or us?
We have a 90-day agreement review cycle. Can your proof of value finish before our lawyers finish reading?

metrics.speaker: Head of Model Risk (MRM)
metrics.partial: We track false positives on fraud review queues, but nobody has agreed on a target yet.
metrics.verbatim: We will only move forward if the agent cuts false-positive fraud alerts below 2 percent without raising missed fraud.

economic_buyer.speaker: CIO
economic_buyer.partial: The budget sits with my platform group, but the business owner wants to co-sign anything above our threshold.
economic_buyer.verbatim: I hold the platform budget and I sign the PO myself up to the cap. Anything above that goes to the Chief Risk Officer.

decision_criteria.speaker: CISO
decision_criteria.partial: Security and model risk have their own checklists, and they weight them differently.
decision_criteria.verbatim: We score every vendor on zero data retention, sub-processor disclosure, bring-your-own keys, and audit logs. A vendor that fails zero retention is out, regardless of price.

decision_process.speaker: CIO
decision_process.partial: There is a committee review, then legal, then a sign-off, and the order sometimes changes.
decision_process.verbatim: The order is committee review, then InfoSec, then Model Risk, then legal redlines, then procurement signs. Legal alone takes about 90 days.

paper_process.speaker: CISO
paper_process.partial: Legal will want changes to the data processing agreement, and that takes a while.
paper_process.verbatim: Our agreement redlines run 90 days minimum. If you want to be live this quarter, InfoSec has to start in parallel with your proof of value.

identify_pain.speaker: Head of Model Risk (MRM)
identify_pain.partial: Our analysts spend too long clearing alerts that turn out to be nothing.
identify_pain.verbatim: Our last audit had forty-one open findings on manual alert review, and I cannot keep adding analysts to close them.

champion.speaker: Head of Model Risk (MRM)
champion.partial: I think this could help my team, and I am willing to push it internally.
champion.verbatim: I will carry this to the risk committee myself, and I need a validation pack I can defend in front of the examiners.

competition.speaker: CIO
competition.partial: We have looked at the big cloud providers' built-in options too.
competition.verbatim: We are also evaluating a cloud-native option our platform group already licenses, so you have to beat its price and its auditability.
